events.title: [CRITICAL] PHP2Shell: What to know about two critical PHP flaws
events.summary: CISA has added two critical PHP vulnerabilities, a memory corruption flaw and a stale internal request-state flaw, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog, and a proof-of-concept exploit has been released. Both flaws are rated critical with a CVSS of 9.2 and near-maximum EPSS scores, indicating high exploitation likelihood.

The extremely high EPSS scores and availability of a proof-of-concept make rapid patching urgent for anyone running PHP. A third related vulnerability was also added to KEV the next day.

Defenders should treat the affected extension as compromised and check developer environments for signs of the backdoor.

events.why_it_matters: All three chained CVEs are listed in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, indicating active exploitation risk. The main issue has a CVSS score of 7.0, while one chained bug scores 8.6 with a high EPSS value, so defenders should prioritise patching and monitoring Ivanti Connect Secure devices. A local authenticated attacker could use the flaw to gain higher privileges on affected systems.

events.title: The Mean Lied: How a Second Statistic Fixed Long-Context Memory
events.summary: A community article describes a Princeton paper that identifies a flaw in memory-efficient language models: when a router only uses average relevance scores, it can fail to distinguish a document chunk containing the exact needed fact from one with only vaguely related words. The paper proposes adding variance-based second-order routing to improve long-context memory performance.
events.why_it_matters: For people who build or deploy long-context AI systems, this points to a concrete limitation in current memory-efficient models: average relevance alone can split attention evenly and dilute answers with irrelevant content. The proposed variance-based routing offers a possible way to improve retrieval accuracy, though it is presented as a paper finding rather than a proven deployed solution.

events.title: Florida warns that 4.9 million people had Social Security numbers leaked in financial aid site breach

events.why_it_matters: The scale of the exposure, involving Social Security numbers for nearly five million people, creates a significant identity-theft risk for affected individuals. It also highlights the sensitivity of data held by public education agencies and the consequences when such systems are compromised.

events.title: TeamViewer Flaw Lets Remote Computers Attack Users Who Connect to Control Them
events.summary: TeamViewer patched a vulnerability in which a compromised or malicious remote host could attack the computer running the viewer, potentially crashing the TeamViewer client and, on some platforms, executing code on it.
events.why_it_matters: This matters because remote-control software is often trusted implicitly, so a compromised host can turn a support or access session into an attack against the administrator's own machine. The possibility of code execution on the viewer means defenders should confirm TeamViewer is patched and treat hosts as untrusted. The record gives no CVSS score or evidence of exploitation.

events.title: CVE-2026-115893 — Wasmtime is a runtime for WebAssembly. Prior to 36.0.19, 48.0.7, and 49.0.4, the Cranelift compiler backend on aarch64 can compile a Wasm br
events.summary: (vendor/severity tags below are heuristic) Wasmtime is a runtime for WebAssembly. Prior to 36.0.19, 48.0.7, and 49.0.4, the Cranelift compiler backend on aarch64 can compile a Wasm br_table instruction with more than approximately 256,000 targets so that it has an incorrect conditional branch target. The branch can then jump to arbitrary other code at a user-controlled offset, allowing a user-controlled Wasm module to escape the sandbox on aarch64 engines using the default Cranelift backend. This issue is fixed in versions 36.0.19, 48.0.7, and 49.0.4.

events.summary: This article explains what intrusion detection and prevention systems can and cannot do, warning that simply deploying them does not protect an organisation. It draws on the Equifax, Target, and SolarWinds incidents to argue that detection only reduces harm when monitoring coverage, maintenance, and response processes are in place.
events.why_it_matters: For defenders, the article reinforces that security tooling is only as effective as the operations around it: alerts require authorised staff to act, and configuration, logging, and detection rules need ongoing upkeep. events.why_it_matters: This is a small example of an on-device, open-source AI tool for a personal memorial task; builders may see it as a pattern for running AI locally rather than through cloud services. It also shows AI being applied to emotional and memorial contexts, not only technical or business workflows.

events.title: I built a way to see where your AI budget goes
events.summary: A developer shared a new tool, ModelFare, to forecast AI spending before launch by considering extra costs beyond per-token pricing, such as repeated attempts, tool use and backup models.
events.why_it_matters: For teams building on AI, total spend can be higher than token prices suggest because retries, tool calls and fallback models add up. Tools like this aim to make those costs visible during planning rather than after deployment. The post is an announcement and contains no security or regulatory details.

events.title: HALLOWEEN FOLKLORE AI
events.summary: A developer built and shared a minimalist web app for Hacktoberfest that uses Google Apps Script, Wikipedia, and Hugging Face's inference API to generate Halloween folklore for whatever keyword a user enters.
events.why_it_matters: For AI builders, the post shows a lightweight pattern: a script-hosted UI can call Wikipedia for source text and a hosted model API for curation, avoiding a custom backend. No security incidents, vulnerabilities, or policy implications are described in the record.

events.title: Identifying election domain threats before they become attacks
events.summary: New research on election-related domains warns that lookalike domains can be used for impersonation and that defenders must separate real threats from false alarms.
events.why_it_matters: For organisations securing election activity, the research highlights domain impersonation as a risk and shows that detection systems need to distinguish genuine malicious lookalikes from benign false positives.

events.title: CVE-2026-116682 — FileBrowser Quantum is a free, self-hosted, web-based file manager. Prior to 1.5.2-stable and 2.0.1-beta, file read handling in backend/pkg/
events.summary: A high-severity path traversal vulnerability (CVE-2026-116682) was disclosed in FileBrowser Quantum, a self-hosted web-based file manager. Versions before 1.5.2-stable and 2.0.1-beta mishandle symbolic links during file reads, allowing an authenticated user with download access to reach files outside their authorised scope, and fixed releases are available.
events.why_it_matters: The flaw carries a CVSS of 8.6 from the CNA and was rated high severity, though it is not listed in KEV and has a low EPSS score. Any organisation running the affected versions should upgrade, since symlink-based reads across download, preview, media, OnlyOffice and public-share flows can expose server-accessible files to ordinary authenticated users.

events.title: [HIGH] CVE-2026-117540 — svg-sanitizer from 0.5.3 before 1.1.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability in Sanitizer::sanitize() that repeatedly rescans the whole
events.summary: A high-severity denial of service flaw (CVE-2026-117540) has been reported in the svg-sanitizer PHP library affecting versions 0.5.3 to before 1.1.0. An unauthenticated attacker can submit crafted SVG files containing many overlapping PHP tag openers and closers, causing the sanitizer's cleanup routine to repeatedly rescan the whole input and consume CPU for extended periods.
events.why_it_matters: The flaw carries a CVSS score of 8.7 and is rated high severity, meaning applications using this library could be forced offline by anyone who can upload an SVG, without needing credentials or exploit code publicised so far. It is not listed in KEV and its EPSS score is low, suggesting exploitation is not yet widespread. Defenders running PHP applications that sanitise SVG uploads should check whether they use an affected version and plan an upgrade to 1.1.0 or later.
